title: Perception: Perceptual Constancies, Illusions, Color Vision
summary: Perceptual constancies (shape, size, brightness); optical illusions (Müller-Lyer, Necker cube, Ponzo, Hermann grid, Hering); trichromatic theory; opponent process theory; color blindness.
objectives: Compare trichromatic and opponent process theories.
revision: Perceptual constancies: shape, size, brightness. Illusions: Müller-Lyer (length), Necker cube (reversible), Ponzo (size). Color: trichromatic (RGB cones) vs opponent process (red-green, blue-yellow, black-white).
confusions: Believing all illusions are the same type.

r: Perceive shape as constant despite changing retinal image
Perceive size as constant despite distance
Perceive brightness as constant despite illumination
Equal lines appear different due to arrowheads
Equal lines appear different over converging lines

notes.t: Young-Helmholtz trichromatic theory proposes three cone types (red, green, blue) whose combined responses produce all color perceptions.
Opponent process theory proposes color processing in opponent pairs: red-green, blue-yellow, black-white.

r: All three cones present but one functions poorly

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about Müller-Lyer, Necker cube, Ponzo illusions and trichromatic vs opponent process theories.

mnemonics.title: RGB-OY
mnemonics.text: Trichromatic: R — Red, G — Green, B — Blue cones. Opponent: O — Red/Green, Y — Blue/Yellow, K — Black/White.

flashcards.a: Three cone types: red, green, blue.
